title: Private deployment: customer-supplied custom operator caused quantized-model crash loop — safety constraints & rollback playbook
creator: Miguel Torres
summary: A customer-uploaded custom operator binary for an on-prem/private deployment was ABI-incompatible with Redwood's quantized kernels, causing memory corruption and crash loops on model serving hosts. This ticket consolidates the incident timeline, immediate mitigations, and a prioritized set of follow-ups to prevent recurrence and safely re-enable custom ops for private customers.
incident_timeline:
2026-03-09T02:04Z: First alert from pagerduty — multiple model-serving pods restarted rapidly and latency spiked.
2026-03-09T02:07Z: Ops team isolated cluster in eu-west-1-private and paused new uploads.
2026-03-09T02:20Z: Initial triage found repeated SIGSEGVs in quantized attention kernel (addr sanitizer not enabled on prod).
2026-03-09T03:00Z: Customer reported they had pushed a custom operator tarball as part of an integration; operator name overlapped with an internal op name.
2026-03-09T04:10Z: Reproduced crash locally using customer's operator binary with quantized model; root cause traced to signature mismatch and unexpected memory layout.
2026-03-09T05:00Z: Emergency mitigation: disabled customer operator loading on affected private clusters and rolled affected model deployments to non-quantized fallback variants.
2026-03-09T07:30Z: Cluster stabilized; service restored to normal latency and error rates.
root_cause: Customer-supplied operator binary registered an operator name colliding with Redwood's internal op, but used a different calling convention and memory layout optimized for a different quant packing format. When the inference runtime selected a quant-optimized kernel, the operator invoked mismatched code paths leading to memory corruption and crash loops. Lack of strict operator ABI/version validation and absence of sandboxing for third-party ops allowed the faulty binary to run in the serving process.
immediate_remediation: 1) Blocked custom operator loading for all private clusters and notified customers. 2) Rolled back affected model routes to float/int8 variants without the third-party op dependency. 3) Deployed hotfix that refuses operator registrations with duplicate names and logs callsite stack traces for any attempted overloads. 4) Added emergency alert for >5 restarts per pod in 10m and op-fallback-rate >2%.
long_term_action_items: Implement operator namespace/versioning: require OPNAME@semantic_version on upload and refuse bare names.
Build a binary validation pipeline that runs uploaded op binaries in a hermetic sandbox with ABI fuzz tests and memory-safety checks before enabling on any serving hosts.
Add operator isolation: load third-party ops into a jailed process and use IPC to invoke them; fall back to safe internal implementation on failure.

Enhance model canaries: when a private customer uploads ops or model variants, run a quantized canary suite including randomized sequence lengths and parity checks versus non-quantized reference outputs to detect accuracy drift or crashes.
Upgrade runtime to fail-fast on op signature mismatches and emit structured diagnostics to logs and the console (op_name, expected_sig, observed_sig, stacktrace).
Document permitted op interfaces and publish a lightweight SDK to help customers build compatible ops.
Create an RBAC restriction for enabling custom ops on private clusters and require an onboarding checklist + security signoff for early-access customers.
owner_notes: Priority is to re-enable safe custom op usage for paying private customers without exposing other tenants or risking production crash loops. Primary owner: Miguel Torres, secondary: Priya Shah.

2026-03-10 SRE Lead - Liam Chen: Added emergency alert for pod restart storm and increased retention on crash logs for five affected hosts. Dashboard: see links.
